Subject: Quiet demo nook request for CloudWave meetings (Hall 3 - B12)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for walking the hall with me yesterday. CloudWave is planning a series of closed-door product walkthroughs at the show and we wanted to request a small ‘quiet demo nook’ directly adjacent to our B12 footprint in Hall 3. Key asks: 

- Enclosed (three-sided) acoustic panels, ~8ft high, leaving one open side to the aisle for fire marshal compliance
- 1 x 20A power drop (for laptop demo & small monitor) + dedicated ethernet drop if possible
- Two high-top tables + four guest stools and one small host chair
- Minimal branding on the panel exteriors — brand vinyl on the inside only

Attached is a rough sketch of the requested layout and our preferred adjacency to the walkline. Can you confirm whether this is feasible in the B12 location and if there are any sightline or height restrictions we should plan for? Also, please confirm lead times and any surcharges from show services so we can add to our budget.

Thanks,
Jared

On Wed, May 7, 2028 at 09:14 Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Looping in Laura and Rishi to validate sightline and utilities constraints.
>
Thanks for the context — read the sketch and floor plan. A few show-specific constraints to be aware of: 

1) Height/sightlines: Hall 3 show rules cap temporary partitions at 8ft measured from floor to top for inline/nook builds in aisle-adjacent locations. For island booths the cap is 10ft but B12 is considered an inline-adjacent placement because of the neighboring shell scheme. So 8ft is the hard limit.

2) Fire & egress: fully enclosed rooms are allowed only with stamped plans and an exhibitor-supplied fire extinguisher and a site inspection fee. To avoid delays, recommended to keep one open face (as you proposed) and mark a clear egress path.

3) Utilities: current utility map shows a single 20A circuit routed within 12ft of B12. Expo will charge a premium for an additional dedicated run; ops indicated ~48-72 hour lead for ethernet installation.

4) Branding: the show allows branding on interior panels but limits printed surfaces facing primary aisles for sponsor-tier control. If CloudWave needs interior-only vinyl, we’re fine, but exterior facing panels will require pre-approval. See attached brand_guidelines_summary.pdf for internal note on logo clearspace and permitted panel materials.

Next steps I recommend: 
- Order acoustic three-panel assembly (8ft) with open face; specify interior vinyl only.
- Request single 20A + ethernet install now; if ethernet not possible by move-in, arrange a local bonded WiFi hotspot as failover.
- Ask logistics to provide a site visit window for final stake/placement the morning of May 21.

I’ve flagged potential extra costs (~$950) if they require stamped plans for enclosure.

Laura Bennett
Senior Events Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
(Attachment: brand_guidelines_summary.pdf)
